messages:
Priya: Heads up — Sales just handed a POC that wants a Private/VPC deployment scaled from ~10 -> 60 concurrent VPC tenants across a 2-week Black Friday ramp. Core targets: p99 <= 2ms token latency, avg request 400 tokens, peak ~220 req/s aggregated across tenants. Need a quick HW mix + seasonal buffer recommendation for the on-prem racks. Any quick thoughts?

Sam: rough ballpark — if avg req = 400 tokens and we target the stated peak, tokens/s = 220 * 400 = 88k tok/s. Single-tenant H100 fp16 bench ~2.2k tok/s, but with multitenant isolation we discount to ~60% -> ~1.32k usable tok/s per H100. So 88k / 1.32k ≈ 67 H100s. Add ~15% seasonal buffer -> ~77 H100s. This is conservative for sustained peak.

Mateo: perf numbers I have: H100 fp16 ~2.2k tok/s, A100 80GB ~1.1k, L40S ~900. For multitenant steady-state planning use ~55-65% of single-tenant numbers (I use 60% above). So usable: H100 ~1320, A100 ~660, L40S ~540 tok/s.

Jo: watch KV-cache misses. If cache miss rate ~15%, we see 20-30% latency tail increase and more NVMe IOPS/network. Recommend SSD-backed local cache per rack (NVMe) and 100Gb rack uplink minimum.

Sam: quick sketch of the calc I ran (very rough):
```
# assumptions
peak_qps = 220
avg_tokens = 400
tokens_per_sec = peak_qps * avg_tokens  # 88k tokens/s
# usable tokens per GPU (multitenant fudge)
H100_usable = 1320  # tokens/s
GPUS_needed = ceil(tokens_per_sec / H100_usable)  # 88k/1320 ~ 67 => 67 H100s
seasonal_buffer = 0.15
total_with_buffer = ceil(GPUS_needed * (1+seasonal_buffer))  # ~77 H100s
```
Note: if customer accepts A100s, expect ~2x GPU count. If mixed fleet, adjust accordingly.

Carla: customer budget prefers a mixed fleet. They want lower cost than an all-H100 baseline. Could we propose hot-path H100s + cheaper cards for background tasks? Maybe a 50/30/20 split?

Mateo: that split maps roughly to: 50% H100s for low-latency frontends, 30% A100s for mid-latency workloads, 20% L40S/T4 for async/batch. For the ~77-GPU baseline that becomes ~38 H100, 23 A100, 16 L40S (rounded). That keeps p99 goals for interactive traffic while lowering cost for bulk inference.

Priya: region/ networking constraints — customer will place racks in two DCs (AMS + FRA). Do they need sync KV replication? If yes, inter-DC bandwidth is important.

Jo: recommend async replication with frequent checkpoints for most VPCs. If they require strong consistency (rare), plan for 25-40 Gbps interconnect per DC-pair at peak plus higher cross-DC tail budgets. Async reduces continuous load and cost.

Sam: power & facility note: an H100 ~700W draw; factor PDU/cooling overhead ~1.6x -> ~1.1kW per GPU. 77 GPUs -> ~85kW steady, plan PDUs/racks accordingly. Also plan NVMe capacity: suggest 4x read-optimized NVMes per rack (e.g., 1.6TB each) in RAID for cache hot-paths.

Priya: Ops/action items: Mateo + Sam to produce a one-pager + CSV sizing template (per-rack) with knobs: target p99, avg tokens, concurrency, seasonal buffer %. Use this customer as example. Jo to add network & cache config. Carla to confirm SLA & budget sweet spot.

Mateo: will draft template and push to internal doc at https://redwood.internal/private-sizes. Expect a first pass EOD tomorrow. I'll include a per-rack CSV with columns: rack_id, gpu_type, gpus_count, usable_tok_per_sec, nvme_count, uplink_gbps, est_power_kw.

Sam: additional optimization note — if customer can shard tenants by model family and run cache warmers to reduce cold KV misses, effective tokens/s demand can drop ~20-30%. Worth proposing as a cost-reduction feature.

Carla: customer is open to warmers; I'll flag that in the commercial scope as an optional item to reduce HW cost.

deploy-bot: scheduled reminder — followup sync 2026-11-01 15:00 UTC (created by Priya).  

Priya: thanks everyone. This gives enough to start the quote. If any objections to the H100-heavy baseline, say now. Otherwise I'll finalize the template and pass to Sales. :thumbsup:
